trajectory_summary: This is a warm, customer-initiated callback that stayed pleasant throughout but never tightened into a structured qualification or a locked appointment. The rep held scope discipline well and correctly navigated a landline obstacle, but let a long personal/weather/travel rapport tangent run without redirecting back to the bill capture or a scheduled callback time. The call ends on goodwill with no bill in hand and no specific day/time booked.
outcome_dispute: The call is best read as a callback/soft-open lead, not a booked or tentative appointment — no day or time was stated, and the next step is contingent on the customer sending a bill photo whenever he gets to it. If v1 tagged this as booked or tentative, that overstates the state of commitment reached.

observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time is ever stated; the rep frames the next phone call as something to be scheduled later, contingent on the customer sending back a bill photo, which makes this a callback-pending-artifact outcome rather than a booked or tentative appointment.

key_moments.stewart_read: Rep states the correct 670 threshold matching schema, and runs the title/co-owner qualifier in the same breath, though he never separately asks if anyone else is on the title as its own question.

key_moments.stewart_read: This is a plausible pro-solar motivational signal — grievance against the utility could be leveraged as a reason-to-act — but it's expressed as anti-utility politics rather than a clear stated interest in solar, so it should be read as a possible signal, not a confirmed one.
